review.title: Review
review.offBody: Read a note once and it fades in a few days. Review brings it back on the day you are closest to forgetting it. Not every note every day — only what is needed that day.
review.offSample: When was the Ottoman Empire founded :: 1299
review.offBody2: Write a line like that in a note and it becomes a question. Or tag a note with #tekrar and the whole note comes back for you to re-read. Nothing you have not marked ever enters review.
review.onVacation: You are on holiday mode, nothing is due today. Change the end date in settings.
review.noCards: No marked notes yet. Write a line like "Question :: Answer" in a note, or tag it #tekrar.
review.allDone: Done for today. You studied {{n}} cards, see you tomorrow.
review.deferredNote: {{n}} of them fell outside your limit and move to tomorrow.
review.easedNote: Today is an easy day, so the count was reduced.
review.newPausedNote: New cards are paused until the backlog clears.
review.backlogSub: You do not have to finish them in one day. I can spread them out.
review.forecastHint: Busiest day is {{peak}} cards. A flat line means the load is even.
review.sessionDoneSub: Tomorrow you pick up where you left off.

set.enableSub: When off, nothing is scanned and no files are created in your vault.
set.cardCount: You currently have {{n}} marked cards in your notes.
set.estFits: Your limit is {{cap}}. It fits comfortably — even at the busiest, about {{min}} minutes a day.
set.estOver: You set the limit to {{cap}} but at the busiest {{need}} cards come out per day. {{over}} extra cards move to the next day; if the backlog grows I stop showing new cards by myself.
set.estToday: {{n}} cards ready for today, about {{min}} minutes.
set.presetSub: Pick one and I will set the rest.
set.retentionSub: How often you want to remember a card when I ask. Lower it and cards come less often, so daily work drops.
set.retLow: I ask rarely; you will forget sometimes, but daily work is light.
set.retHigh: I ask often; you will almost never forget, but daily work grows.
set.minutesSub: I measure your answer times and trim the queue to fit. Enter 0 for no time limit.
set.easyDaysSub: Tap a day: normal → half → off. Cards from an off day spread to neighbouring days.
set.vacationSub: Nothing comes up until this date, and it does not count as a backlog.
set.newPerDaySub: At most how many never-seen cards arrive each day.
set.newIgnoresSub: When off, new cards stop by themselves during a backlog and resume once it clears. Turn it on and new cards arrive every day.
set.balanceSub: I move a card to the emptiest day inside a small window. It does not break the interval.
set.burySub: So the same topic is not asked back to back, the note's remaining cards move to tomorrow.
set.orderRisk: Most likely to be forgotten first
set.leechAtSub: If you forget a card this many times the card itself is the problem; it probably needs splitting.
set.syn_reverse_sub: Becomes two cards: forward and back
set.syn_block_sub: Question, a lone question mark, answer
set.syn_cloze_sub: Text between double equals is hidden
set.syn_note_sub: A note with this tag comes back for you to re-read
set.noFolders: No folders in your vault yet.
set.algoSub: The new method tracks how settled a card is and does not reset it when you forget. The old one is simpler.
set.learnSteps: How many times to ask a new card the same day
set.learnStepsSub: Write minutes separated by spaces. Example: 1 10
set.relearnSteps: How many times to ask a forgotten card the same day
set.maxIntervalSub: A card is never asked less often than this.
set.estHint: This is the highest load you would reach if you keep adding notes at this pace. Today's real number is below.

help.title: Help & Guide
help.subtitle: Learn Loomen in a few minutes — everything is simple and fully local.
help.filesBody: Every note is a plain .md (Markdown) file on your computer. No internet or server; everything stays on your device. Even if you delete a note it first goes to the Trash (kept for 30 days), so you won't lose it by accident.
help.createBody: Press ⌘N to create a new note. Press ⌘O to jump to or search for an existing one. Use the Explorer on the left to browse your folders, and drag notes to reorganize them.
help.linksBody: To connect two notes, type the note's name inside double square brackets in your text. It becomes a clickable link and shows up in the Graph as a line between two dots. This is how you build a web between your notes.
help.tagsBody: Write a tag starting with # inside a note (e.g. #journal). Notes that share a tag become related. In the Graph, tags appear as green nodes that connect every note using them.
help.graphBody: The Graph is a map of your notes: dots are notes, lines are links, green nodes are tags. Drag to move around, scroll to zoom, click a dot to open the note. Use + / − on the right to zoom and the target icon to fit the graph to the screen; the settings icon toggles tags, orphan notes and arrows.
help.plannerBody: The Planner keeps your daily tasks, calendar and focus timer (Pomodoro) in one place. The 'Today's Note' button at the top opens today's note. Complete tasks with a checkbox, give them dates, and drag to reorder. Focus while the Pomodoro runs, then rest on the break.
help.drawBody: The Draw screen lets you make freehand sketches and diagrams (Excalidraw). The Reports screen shows summary statistics about your notes and tasks.
help.syncBody: Loomen has no server of its own. Because your notes are plain files, you can sync them across devices with iCloud Drive, Syncthing or Git. Backing up your vault folder means backing up all of your data.
help.safetyBody: Loomen never touches your notes' content silently. Moving and renaming preserve the file exactly; deleting is always reversible. The single source of truth is the file on your disk.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.consent: While off, no AI request is made at all. Once enabled, your question and the content of the open note are sent to the provider you choose. To stay fully offline, pick "OpenAI compatible" and point it at a local address such as Ollama.
ai.appOnly: The assistant only works in the desktop and mobile app.
ai.activeProviderSub: This provider is used in chat; you can also switch it from the assistant screen.
ai.addProviderSub: You can add several providers and switch between them.
ai.startHint: Ask something about the note you have open.
ai.offHint: The assistant is off. Enable it in settings and add a provider.
ai.noProviderHint: No provider added yet. Add a provider and API key in settings.
ai.scopeHint: The assistant finds the note sections relevant to your question and sends only those.
ai.showContextSettingSub: Under each answer you can see exactly what was sent to the provider.
ai.excludedSub: Notes in these folders are never read and never sent to the provider.
ai.geminiFree: Google Gemini's free tier is enough for this.
